title.narrative: Output 5.1. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative: Following the development of the 2018-2022 National Strategic Framework (NSF) for technical and vocational education and training (TVET), which seeks to improve the relevance of TVET training to labour market demand in Lebanon, the Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) implemented core actions as outlined in the NSF. A policy brief was developed to highlight the importance of addressing the pronounced skills mismatch in the agricultural labour market while also providing an assessment of specific skills in demand. This brief served as one of the core foundations for the Government of Lebanon in developing its National Agriculture Strategy 2020-2025. The ILO, in partnership with FAO and with support from Norway, led the development of the policy brief through focus group discussions with the private sector to identify the trends of supply and demand in terms of skills needed in various agricultural value chains. This was the first skills development study for the sector. The ILO also introduced tracer study mechanisms within the MoA to evaluate systematically the employment impact of its programmes, its gender implications, and gather employers and graduates feedback on the relevance and quality of the training. The ILO conducted a tracer study of 363 graduates to assess employment outcomes, which was then followed by the revision of occupational standards and curricula: This will also guide the MoA to develop occupational standards for other occupations as per labour market demand.

Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Agriculture (MoA) has institutionalized its engagement with the private sector to promote quality work-based learning and apprenticeship opportunities, ensuring that its programmes and graduates meet the skills requirements needed by industry to ultimately contribute to employment generation and poverty reduction.
A Code of Conduct for employers implementing work-based learning programmes was issued and is utilized by government, schools and the livelihood sector. It provides standards that employers should meet to ensure a safe learning environment for trainees.
Improved understanding and overall capacity of the trainees in implementing or supporting implementation of competency based training is reported. The ILO, in partnership with FAO and with support from Norway, facilitated the development of a draft agreement between MoA and the private sector in collaboration with the Federation of the Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture, to promote international good practices related to on-the-job training to its members.
The Code of Conduct was developed by ILO, UNICEF and the Ministry of Labour (MoL) through ILO-led consultations in 2019-2020 with FAO, business and employer organizations, trade unions, the MoA and the livelihood sector.
The ILO further supported the capacity building of stakeholders in the areas of work-based learning and apprenticeships, among other topics, through an e-learning Skills Academy, in response to COVID-19, in partnership with ITC-ILO. A total of 175 participants from 35 organizations registered for the Skills Academy and 58% enrolled in at least one course (61% women), with a 74% overall completion rate. Organizations included ministries of Education, Agriculture, Labour, and Social Affairs, as well as the Chamber of Commerce, the Association of Lebanese industrialists, the Confederation of Trade Unions, TVET institutions, NGOs active in the sector and UN agencies.

title.narrative: 5.3.1. Number of member States that have applied ILO approaches to work-based learning and quality apprenticeships
Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Agriculture (MoA), its local schools and implementing partners, completed vocational training in two in-demand occupations for 48 students (46% girls, 21% Non-Lebanese) including the piloting of enhanced on-the-job (OJT) toolkits.
The Ministry of Agriculture and the Agriculture Training Centers in Akkar and Bekaa developed 4 competency based (CB) assessment tools and 2 CB curricula for Agriculture Machine repairer and Livestock/ Dairy farmer. The ILO, in partnership with FAO and with support from Norway, led the development of OJT tools for two occupations, from which further training programmes for specific occupations have been developed and institutionalized by MoA and its partners.
Two occupations for CB development were decided based on the skills mismatch study conducted by ILO, which fits the labour market needs in the current times and was validated by a private sector field assessment in both regions.
